question: At every exposed R10AP partial-recovery pose, can existing contacts support weight in a stationary surrogate with the existing actuator bounds, and what minimum nonfoot support does the model require?

population.selection: Every partial-recovery observation, including terminal, in original order.

model.generalized_velocity: World root translation and rotation plus eight canonical hip/knee velocities; 14 coordinates.
model.gravity: Use retained direct-state gravity, body masses and body COM positions. Check mass-weighted COM against the controller observation within 1e-6 m.
model.jacobian: Root columns I and axis cross point-minus-root. Joint columns are normalized measured parent z-axis cross point-minus-measured-parent-side-hinge; only ancestor joints contribute.
model.contact_population: Retained strictly positive normal-impulse contacts, both foot and nonfoot; use original reported world points, preserve original classification. No invented or newly enabled contacts.
model.friction: Authored coefficient, used as an explicit model assumption. Upward world-y normals; inner friction pyramid abs(fx)+abs(fz)<=1.8*fy and fy>=0. This is not a claim about exact native combined-material or moving-friction response.
model.actuator_limits: Published per-step impulse divided by the unchanged 1/120 s outer timestep; symmetric canonical torque bounds. No command or cap is changed.
model.objective: First certify equilibrium feasibility. For feasible problems minimize total nonfoot upward force divided by measured total weight.
model.staging_limit: Reported contact points are retained at native contact-sampling time while body/joint frames are callback states. This frozen-frame surrogate does not remove that staging difference or finite constraint deformation.
model.dynamics_excluded: No mass-matrix acceleration, Coriolis terms, passive joint-limit forces, impulse-to-force reconstruction, contact creation, trajectory propagation, or actual static-state assertion.

numerics.phase_one: Normalize each generalized balance row by max(1,abs(gravity_row)). Minimize sum of positive and negative equilibrium slacks, leaving friction and torque bounds enforced. A certified optimum above 1e-7 is a model infeasibility result.
numerics.certificate: Check primal feasibility, dual signs, stationarity, complementary slackness and primal-dual objective gap for every solve. Recheck unscaled balances on every feasible load distribution.

checks: Eight known-answer controls covering force/moment balance, unsupported moment, required nonfoot load fraction, and bounded actuator infeasibility before retained evaluation.
Independent contact-source replay and body mass/COM reconstruction for all 601 samples.
Retain all 1803 model outcomes, their phase-I certificates, and every feasible force/torque allocation.
No tuning of variants, friction, caps, objectives or tolerances after result exposure.

research_sources.use: Generalized manipulator equations and contact Jacobian transpose forces.
Static equilibrium and unilateral Coulomb friction constraints.
Pinned installed-version dual-simplex interface and marginal conventions.
